words.g: m. nom. sg. of ऋषि (i-stem); subject of उवाच
√वच् (adādi, 2P ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

sandhi.note: The final s of ऋषिस् becomes ru. After a vowel other than a/ā and before a vowel it is not turned into visarga (खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः, 8.3.15, applies only at a pause or before an unvoiced consonant), so it stands as r and joins the next word: ṛṣir uvāca.

morph.note: Perfect of √वच् with samprasāraṇa in the reduplicating syllable (व → उ): ‘(he) said’, the narrative past.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: The hymn of Indra and the gods (4.2–27) is over, and Medhas, the seer, resumes his narration to King Suratha and the merchant Samādhi. What follows is the close of the Madhyama Carita: the Goddess’s answer to the hymn and the boons the gods ask.

words.g: indeclinable (adverb of manner); refers back to the hymn 4.2–27

m. instr. pl. of सुर; agent of स्तुता (and, understood, of अर्चिता)
n. instr. pl. of दिव्य; qualifies कुसुमैः
n. instr. pl. of कुसुम; instrument of अर्चिता
n. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies कुसुमैः

n. gen. pl. of जगत्; depends on धात्री
f. nom. sg. of धात्री (√धा + tṛc, feminine in -ī); the subject, carried into 4.30 (प्राह)
indeclinable (connective adverb)
n. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); instrument of अर्चिता

sandhi.note: A word-final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra. The same gives जगतां धात्री.
After ai (a vowel other than a/ā) the final s becomes ru and stays r before the voiced d. The same in कुसुमैर्नन्दनोद्भवैः.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (vyadhikaraṇa: the members are in different cases)
samasa.sense: flowers from Nandana, the garden of Indra’s heaven
samasa.alt: It could be taken as a pañcamī tatpuruṣa with उद्भव in the sense ‘sprung’ (नन्दनात् उद्भवः); but उद्भव is an action noun ‘origin’, so the bahuvrīhi is the natural analysis. The sense is the same.

samasa.sense: fragrant substances and anointing pastes, two of the offerings of worship
samasa.alt: Also possible as a tatpuruṣa, ‘with fragrant unguents’ (गन्धयुक्तानि अनुलेपनानि); with तथा marking a further class of offering, the dvandva reads more naturally.

morph.note: √स्तु is aniṭ: the participle takes -ta directly (स्तुत), feminine स्तुता.
√अर्च् takes the connecting -i- (iṭ): अर्चित, feminine अर्चिता. Both participles are passive and agree with the Goddess as subject.
Agent noun धातृ ‘one who holds, supports’ (√धा + tṛc) made feminine with -ī: ‘sustainer’; in common usage also ‘nurse, foster-mother’.

mantras.anvaya: एवं सुरैः स्तुता, दिव्यैः नन्दनोद्भवैः कुसुमैः तथा गन्धानुलेपनैः अर्चिता जगतां धात्री (4.30 … प्राह)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The sentence runs into 4.30: two participial phrases (स्तुता …, अर्चिता …) describe the subject जगतां धात्री, whose verb is प्राह in the next verse.
mantras.lit: Thus praised by the gods, worshipped with heavenly flowers grown in Nandana, and likewise with perfumes and unguents, the sustainer of the worlds —
mantras.tr: Praised in this way by the gods, and honoured with heavenly flowers from the garden of Nandana, with perfumes and with fragrant pastes, the Mother of the worlds —
mantras.tr_note: धात्री is rendered ‘Mother’, its common sense of nurse and sustainer; the sentence is completed in 4.30.

comm.t: Medhas describes what followed the hymn: the gods do not stop at words but worship the Goddess with flowers from Nandana, Indra’s pleasure-garden, and with perfumes and unguents. The incense follows in 4.30.

Flowers, fragrance and (in the next verse) incense are among the standard upacāras of pūjā. In the story the gods perform for the Goddess the worship that her devotees go on to offer when the text is recited.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the name जगद्धात्री (935), ‘sustainer of the world’; the Devī Māhātmya says the same in two words, जगतां धात्री. The two texts remain separate works.

प्र + √ब्रू (adādi, 2U ‘to speak’) with the substitute stem आह्; laṭ, prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; used as a narrative past

sandhi.note: One run of four instrumentals shows both outcomes of a visarga after ai: before the unvoiced t it becomes s (समस्तैस्, धूपैस्); before the voiced d and dh the ru stays r (त्रिदशैर्, दिव्यैर्).

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi of prefix and verb (savarṇa-dīrgha)
sandhi.note: The prefix प्र joins the verb आह: a + ā → ā.
Final n before p and s needs no change; the Gita Press prints the n with a virāma and a space.

samasa.vigraha: त्रिः आवृत्ताः दश परिमाणम् एषाम्, तैः
samasa.literal: those whose count is three tens
samasa.sense: the gods, the ‘Thirty’, a round figure for the thirty-three gods of the Veda
samasa.alt: A traditional etymology reads तृतीया दशा (यौवनम्) येषां ते, ‘those who are ever in the third stage of life (youth)’, i.e. the ageless gods; also a bahuvrīhi. The numerical reading is the usual one.

samasa.vigraha: प्रसादेन सुमुखी (सुमुखी = शोभनं मुखं यस्याः सा)
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, its second member a bahuvrīhi
samasa.sense: her face showing her pleasure and grace
samasa.alt: Also read as a pañcamī (cause) relation, प्रसादात् सुमुखी, ‘fair-faced because pleased’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: आह is the substitute that √ब्रू takes in the present (laṭ) parasmaipada, first five endings (आह, आहतुः, आहुः, आत्थ, आहथुः). It is used in narrative for ‘said’. Some grammarians instead treat आह as a perfect of a defective root अह्; either way it means ‘said’.
Denominative-causative stem धूपय- ‘to perfume with incense’ + kta with iṭ: धूपित, ‘censed’. The cognate noun धूपैः stands beside it (‘censed with incense’).
प्र + √नम् + kta: the nasal is lost before -ta (नत), and n becomes ṇ after प्र: प्रणत, ‘bowed’.

mantras.anvaya: (एवं स्तुता अर्चिता जगतां धात्री) समस्तैः त्रिदशैः भक्त्या दिव्यैः धूपैः तु धूपिता प्रसादसुमुखी (सती) समस्तान् प्रणतान् सुरान् प्राह।
mantras.anvaya_en: The main verb प्राह completes the sentence begun in 4.29; its subject is जगतां धात्री, described by a third participle (धूपिता) and the adjective प्रसादसुमुखी. सुरान् is the person addressed.
mantras.lit: and censed with devotion by all the Thirty with heavenly incenses, she, fair-faced with favour, spoke to all the gods, who were bowed down.
mantras.tr: and when all the gods had devoutly offered her heavenly incense, she, her face bright with grace, spoke to the whole company of gods as they bowed before her.

comm.t: The sentence that began in 4.29 ends here. Praise, flowers, unguents and incense are followed by the Goddess’s favour, which shows on her face (प्रसादसुमुखी). The fierce face that terrified Mahiṣa (4.13) is now a gracious one.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess सुमुखी (459) and सद्यःप्रसादिनी (383, ‘quickly gracious’). The Devī Māhātmya joins the two ideas in one epithet, प्रसादसुमुखी.

words.g: f. nom. sg. of देवी (ī-stem); subject of उवाच
√वच् (adādi, 2P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana

sandhi.note: Final ī before the unlike vowel u becomes y: devy uvāca.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: The Goddess speaks to the gods. In the Madhyama Carita she has spoken once before, the taunt to Mahiṣa before his death (3.37–38); now she speaks to offer a boon.

words.g: √वृ ‘to choose’ (वृङ्, kryādi, 9Ā; also svādi, 5U), karmaṇi prayoga, loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
m. voc. pl. of त्रिदश; compound (see 4.30)
m. voc. pl. of सर्व; qualifies त्रिदशाः
relative pronoun यद्, n. nom. sg.; the grammatical subject of the passive व्रियताम्
ablative in -tas (tasil) of अस्मद्, plural stem; the plural of majesty, the Goddess speaking of herself
past passive participle (kta, with iṭ) of अभि + √वाञ्छ् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to wish’), n. nom. sg.; predicate of यत्

sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.
Final t becomes d before a vowel.
-aḥ before a: the ru becomes u, a + u gives o, and the following a is absorbed into the o (avagraha).

morph.note: Passive imperative: √वृ + yak, with ṛ becoming ri before the passive -ya- (व्रिय-), and the ātmanepada imperative ending -ताम्. ‘Let (whatever is desired) be chosen’ is the courteous form of ‘choose!’.
The suffix -tas (tasil) gives ablative sense to pronouns: मत्तः ‘from me’, अस्मत्तः ‘from us’. The Goddess uses the plural of herself.
अभि + √वाञ्छ् + kta with iṭ: ‘wished for’. Neuter, agreeing with यत्.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) सर्वे त्रिदशाः, यत् अस्मत्तः अभिवाञ्छितम् (तत्) व्रियताम्।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive imperative with a relative clause as its subject: ‘let (that) be chosen which is desired from us’; the correlative तत् is understood.
mantras.lit: Let it be chosen, O all you Thirty, whatever is desired from us.
mantras.tr: All you gods, choose whatever you desire of me.
mantras.tr_note: The passive imperative is rendered as an active ‘choose’, and the plural of majesty (अस्मत्तः) as ‘me’.

comm.t: A half-verse: the Goddess, pleased by the hymn and the worship, offers the gods a boon. This is the classical response of a deity to praise, and it sets up the request that follows (4.34–37).

The same pattern returns at the end of the Uttama Carita: after the hymn to Nārāyaṇī the Goddess says वरदाहं सुरगणा वरं यन्मनसेच्छथ (11.37), and the gods again ask for the destruction of their enemies and the removal of every affliction.
